doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Catskills bebop band and early work at 17
summary: He left a short Blue Cross job for music, playing resort hotel shows in the Catskills.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Did music become your career right away or did you do other things before music?

It seems like it became my career — I guess there were opportunities, whatever it was, when I was about 17. I had a little bebop band in the Catskill mountains, New York, and we were playing [scats] that type thing. So I grew up with that and I think just when I got out of high school I think just for a very short period, six months, I worked for Blue Cross Plan. It was just papers. But then after that it was all music.
Were you playing — when you said you were in the Catskills you said — was it a resort thing?
Yeah. They had all these hotels in the Catskills, and you know at night you played some of the shows, different people, comedians and singers and different things. And you also

could play like some jazz or solo. And so about ten years in the summers I used to go away and I think I once had a piano gig with a vocal group, I played piano. But other times I’d play the flute and saxophone.
Yeah. And I’ll probably skip around here and there sort of on what I was talking about.
